description: Search Jira issues with a JQL query. Returns immediately with a job_id and status 'queued' (D0.3 deferred-completion shape) -- the dispatch returning is NOT the same as the search finishing. When the job completes, trimmed rows (key/summary/status/assignee/updated) are delivered INLINE, one complete result, up to 500 issues by default -- jira carries no PII risk (operator ruling: company-internal accounts only), so this never exports to a file. Atlassian's /search/jql endpoint caps a single HTTP call at 100 issues; within the effective row limit the background job pages internally across that ceiling and hands back one result -- no caller-visible continuation token. At the 500-row default that is up to 5 sequential internal HTTP calls; at the 5,000-row override cap it is up to 50 -- each a real round-trip, so a large row_limit has real latency cost, paid by the background job rather than the dispatch call. Pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true with row_limit to raise the limit above 500, up to 5,000 (above that is refused, never clamped). If more matches exist than the effective limit, truncated is true and total is approximate -- narrow the JQL to see the rest; there is no resume token. Optional fields adds ADDITIONAL columns beyond the fixed render set -- prefer requesting stable ID/status fields over free-text fields when the goal is validation rather than content inspection. Read action.
embedding_description: Find or list Jira issues via a JQL search across a project or the whole site - by assignee, status, recent updates, or a text term. Dispatches asynchronously, returning a job_id immediately; the compact issue rows (key, summary, status, assignee, updated) arrive via job completion, paging internally past Atlassian's 100-per-call ceiling up to a 500-row default.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). This is NOT the issue rows -- those arrive separately when the job completes and are delivered as their own message.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the search was queued -- do not present job_id/status as the answer to the search. Acknowledge the request is in flight; the issue rows land in a follow-up message when the job completes. Once delivered, present the issue rows and row_count. If truncated is true, more matches exist beyond the effective row limit -- say so and suggest narrowing the JQL or raising row_limit (with acknowledge_default_limit_override) rather than implying the result is complete.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Search Jira issues with a JQL query and return the results inline.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: jira.bad_request: the JQL is malformed (unknown field, bad operator, unbalanced quotes) — this is the most common failure on this verb. jira.invalid_params: acknowledge_default_limit_override and row_limit were not both given, or row_limit is not a positive integer, or row_limit exceeds the 5,000 hard cap. jira.auth_failed / jira.permission_denied: the service account's token is invalid/expired or lacks browse permission on the project. jira.not_configured: the jira_site address-book entry is missing or incomplete.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: jira.bad_request: fix the JQL (check field names and quoting) and retry. jira.invalid_params: pass acknowledge_default_limit_override=true together with a row_limit at or below 5,000, or omit both for the 500-row default. jira.auth_failed: the API token may have expired — rotate it (see the jira_plugin overview runbook). jira.not_configured: register the jira_site entry with base_url, email, api_token (vault-ref), and expires_at.
